description: Join the Barony March of Mons Tonitrus for their Combined Fighter Practice, at Arbenz Field in Sierra Vista. (Tacoma St. past the Tennis Courts). Come hone your skills -or pick up a new one- with us! Fight with rattan swords in armor, or fight with a rapier ~ like fencing! Throw axes, knives, or spears at our throwing range! Shoot arrows or a crossbow (and other pointy things!) at our archery range! Loaner equipment is typically available for newcomers. Newcomers must observe park rules AND our safety rules. You can also bring your own equipment and have it inspected by our marshals. Don't feel like fighting? Hang out with our friendly populace, or just enjoy the fresh air and shade in the trees, and cheer on the fighters as they practice. Chat with our Baronial members, or bring a craft you're working on if you like! REMEMBER! Your safety is important to us! The Knight Marshal is in charge of practice, and will be in attendance, maintain the safety of practice, and will make the final call if practice is cancelled (see our Facebook group page about last minute cancellations). For ANYONE in attendance: Everyone signs a liability release WAIVER (managed by the Seneschal and/or Knight Marshal). Always practice caution while on the field, even if spectating or taking pictures. Minors MUST have a parent or legal guardian with them, who can sign a waiver on their behalf. Young children MUST be attended - not dropped off / picked up or ignored. Anyone who is uncooperative with our rules may be asked to leave the field. This is a public park space, to which city rules still apply. Bring water or any beverage that helps you hydrate (such as gatorade). The more the better! Bring a chair if you plan on sitting and resting on something OTHER than grass. Be prepared for the weather (sunglasses, hats, and proper clothing coverage on bright sunny days are a must!). Come early and help us set up the ranges, we start at 9 am! All activities break down around 11:30 am (we MUST have equipment off the field by 12 pm) [RECURRING — also on: 18 Oct 2026, 1 Nov 2026, 15 Nov 2026]

Just wear something comfortable that you can move in (especially comfortable shoes). We meet from 7:30 – 9:30pm at the Holy Trinity Armenian Church, at 145 Brattle Street in Cambridge. There’s a parking lot for those who need to drive, bus routes nearby, and it’s less than a 20 minute walk from the Harvard Square MBTA station. The parking lot is off of Sparks Street, on the far side of the Church away from Brattle Street. (If using a GPS, 62 Sparks Street is roughly across the street from the parking lot.) The hall where we will be dancing is next to the parking lot, so if you are walking up Brattle Street, turn onto Sparks Street to get to the hall. If the front door on Sparks Street is locked, come around to the parking lot side and use the door there. Dances are taught and called using the gender-free “Larks and Robins” style, popular with many of the local dance communities. We have a lot of space (easily twice what we need for dancing), so folks are welcome to come bring other SCA activities for the sidelines, or even to just come hang out! The site costs $100 per session; donations are optional, but welcome to help defray the cost of renting the hall. So come join us! It’s very much “the more, the merrier”, and you’re very welcome to join in! [RECURRING — also on: 27 Oct 2026, 17 Nov 2026]

title: Harvest Market
description: Once a year, the veil between worlds grows thin, and ancient roads, long lost to time, reveal themselves once more. In the hidden places of history—where mysticism, superstition, and the macabre ruled the Middle Ages—a crossroads took root, forged by those who walked the forgotten paths of the thinning veil. Here, at the confluence of worlds, lies a place where treasures are exchanged, memories are honored, and history breathes. As the newly born Mourning Moon ascends, the pathways are open to this archaic place for all to journey. Beyond this threshold, wanderers and traders from the medieval world converge. Viking storytellers, Celtic mystics, Moorish scholars, and Mongol horsemen arrive to share skills, relics, secrets, and stories. Some bring offerings for the dead, others seek wisdom from spirits who linger beyond the veil. The journey will be dangerous, so disguise yourself in attire to blend in with the medieval denizens of this market. You may find yourself learning arts long lost to time, trading tokens from another realm, unearthing forgotten tales by firelight, or discovering the rituals of undiscovered lands. Will you walk among the traders of forgotten civilizations? Carry home a relic from another age? Or leave changed, haunted by whispers of those who once stood in your place? Holiday Market is a hybrid public/private event held in partnership with Mountain Rubn Winery. From 12:00-5:00 pm SCA members and vendors will conduct a demonstration and market open to the public free of charge. The public can take classes and view demonstrations/displays that include archery, thrown weapons, youth combat, arts, sciences, and games. There will be a Halloween-themed costume contest. Food trucks will be on site. At 5:00 the site will be closed to the public for a private SCA event. SCA members, vendors, and non-members who pay the site fee are welcome to stay for a night of revelry. A court and medievel-themed costume contest will begin the evening. From 7:00-9:00 roasted meats, stew, bread, and potatoes will be available for those who pay the feast fee

location: Cozy Craft Room and Studio, 1914 S Power Rd, Mesa, AZ 85206, USA
clean_location: 1914 S Power Rd, Mesa, AZ 85206, USA
description: Taught by Carol of Twin Moons Nalbinding (or nålbinding) is an ancient single-needle textile technique that predates both knitting and crochet. Instead of using a continuous yarn ball with active loops, it uses short, manageable lengths of thread passed entirely through each previous loop to create a durable, non-fraying fabric. It uses a single flat, eyed needle (traditionally bone, wood, or antler) and short lengths of yarn (typically wool). The stitches are formed and tensioned around the crafter’s thumb. New thread lengths are joined by felting the ends together rather than tying knots and because the entire tail of the yarn is pulled through every stitch, the fabric will not unravel or run if cut

description: Greetings traveler! Welcome to the Barony of Twin Moons Weekly meetup. We call it fighter practice, but they are just there to draw everyone’s attention and let the rest of us socialize under the din of their swords clashing! We meet weekly at Gene Autry Park at 7:00 pm (None of us can show up anywhere on time, so it’s really around 7:30 that most folks arrive) on Thursdays. We meet at the middle ramada behind the large playground. When you enter the park, make an immediate right and head past the tennis and volleyball courts. Park at the end and head towards the far ramadas hidden behind the Playground! You can come out and check out Hardsuit and Rapier combat, or you can enjoy chatting with the rest of us who might be there to socialize. This is a regularly occurring social evening for the populace to practice sword fighting as well as chat about whatever we feel like! Once per quarter, there is a Court Night with our epic Quartermoon Tournaments. These will be garbed practices; however, it is not required. This is a great time to show up to meet folks and see what the residents of Atenveldt wear to survive the heat while still looking medieval! Quartermoon Tournaments are set up to help folks learn how tournaments and competitions work within the SCA, so there is very little expectation of skill (which end is the pointy end?). Quartermoon is designed to help you learn so you can become familiar with the way more formal tournaments function at the next event you raid or war you start!! We also sneak in some Arts and Sciences into the event and have a Display setup for folks to show off the cool things they are working on or have finished! Come and share your art and fighting prowess, or just come hang out and enjoy the night with us! Upcoming Dates for Quartermoon fighter practices are November 19, 2026 Upcoming dates for Archery Quartermoon(Sunday before the above dates) November 15, 2026 Archery, for some legal reason, can not happen at City parks, so we do have to relocate our archery practice to Paseo Vista Archery Range 3850 S McQueen Rd, Chandler, AZ 85286 which is still a public park, but they marked out lines in the ground to tell us which way to point the arrows when we let them loose. Times will vary based on the season(heat), so check out the Archery event for times! Come and see us soon and begin your crazy medieval reenactment journey with us! There is no cost to attend practice, and there is no expectation that you have any idea what the SCA is. This is the place for us to meet and show you about our awesome little corner of the world, where we recreate the best parts of the Middle Ages and more! Thanks for checking us out! We call it fighter practice, but they are just there to draw everyone’s attention and let the rest of us socialize under the din of their swords clashing! We meet weekly at Gene Autry Park at 7:00 pm (None of us can show up anywhere on time, so it’s really around 7:30 that most folks arrive) on Thursdays. We meet at the middle ramada behind the large playground. When you enter the park, make an immediate right and head past the tennis and volleyball courts. Park at the end and head towards the far ramadas hidden behind the Playground! You can come out and check out Hardsuit and Rapier combat, or you can enjoy chatting with the rest of us who might be there to socialize. This is a regularly occurring social evening for the populace to practice sword fighting as well as chat about whatever we feel like! Once per quarter, there is a Court Night with our epic Quartermoon Tournaments. These will be garbed practices; however, it is not required. This is a great time to show up to meet folks and see what the residents of Atenveldt wear to survive the heat while still looking medieval! Quartermoon Tournaments are set up to help folks learn how tournaments and competitions work within the SCA, so there is very little expectation of skill (which end is the pointy end?). Quartermoon is designed to help you learn so you can become familiar with the way more formal tournaments function at the next event you raid or war you start!! We also sneak in some Arts and Sciences into the event and have a Display setup for folks to show off the cool things they are working on or have finished! Come and share your art and fighting prowess, or just come hang out and enjoy the night with us! Upcoming Dates for Quartermoon fighter practices are November 19, 2026 Upcoming dates for Archery Quartermoon(Sunday before the above dates) November 15, 2026 Archery, for some legal reason, can not happen at City parks, so we do have to relocate our archery practice to Paseo Vista Archery Range 3850 S McQueen Rd, Chandler, AZ 85286 which is still a public park, but they marked out lines in the ground to tell us which way to point the arrows when we let them loose. Times will vary based on the season(heat), so check out the Archery event for times! Come and see us soon and begin your crazy medieval reenactment journey with us! There is no cost to attend practice, and there is no expectation that you have any idea what the SCA is. This is the place for us to meet and show you about our awesome little corner of the world, where we recreate the best parts of the Middle Ages and more! Thanks for checking us out! title: (Nü) Abendtour durchs Mittelalter / Medieval Night Tour
description: (English below) 🇩🇪🇦🇹🇨🇭 Abendtour durchs Mittelalter Bei unserer Umfrage habt ihr eine Tour durch das mittelalterliche Nürnberg als etwas genannt, das ihr gerne ausprobieren würdet. Also machen wir es einfach einmal. Wir treffen uns vor dem Handwerkerhof, gleich beim Hauptbahnhof, und machen uns von dort auf den Weg durch die Altstadt hinauf zur Kaiserburg. Der direkte Weg wäre etwas langweilig, deshalb machen wir ein paar Umwege durch besonders interessante mittelalterliche Ecken. Adam führt die Tour. Er liebt das mittelalterliche Nürnberg und wurde vor vielen Jahren ein wenig in mittelalterlicher Stadtgeschichte geschult, besonders darin, ihre Spuren in Gebäuden und Straßen zu erkennen. Er wird sein Bestes tun, um alles korrekt zu erzählen, und freut sich über freundliche Korrekturen. Unterhaltsam sollte es auch werden. Er arbeitet schließlich als Comedian und kann wahrscheinlich nicht anders. Du brauchst keine historischen Vorkenntnisse. Du kannst Fragen stellen, eigene Beobachtungen beitragen oder einfach mitkommen und zuhören. Du kannst gerne allein kommen und musst niemanden aus der Gruppe kennen. ⏰ Diesmal ist Pünktlichkeit wichtig: Wir treffen uns um 18:30 Uhr und starten um 18:45 Uhr pünktlich. Wenn du später kommst, verpasst du den Anfang und musst versuchen, uns unterwegs in der Altstadt zu finden. Kurz vor der Veranstaltung teilen wir eine Telefonnummer in der Facebook-Veranstaltung sowie in unserer WhatsApp-Chatgruppe und Infogruppe. Wenn du dich verspätest, ruf bitte dort an oder melde dich über eine der WhatsApp-Gruppen. 👟♿ Wenn du zu Fuß mitkommst, trage bitte bequeme Schuhe. Wenn du einen elektrischen Rollstuhl nutzt, achte bitte auf einen ausreichend geladenen Akku. Die Strecke ist länger, führt bergauf und teilweise über Kopfsteinpflaster. Wir bewegen uns in einem entspannten Tempo und nehmen uns Zeit zum Schauen und Reden. Am Ende suchen wir uns in der Nähe der Kaiserburg oder auf dem Weg hinunter zum Hauptmarkt ein Café, eine Kneipe oder einen anderen gemütlichen Ort. Dort können wir etwas trinken und den Abend ausklingen lassen. Wer nur bei der Tour dabei sein möchte, kann sich natürlich vorher verabschieden. Bei schlechtem Wetter versuchen wir es zunächst mit Regenschirmen. Bitte bring deinen eigenen mit. Wenn die Tour keinen Spaß mehr macht, suchen wir uns stattdessen ein Café und verbringen den Rest des Abends dort. 📅 Wann: 20. Oktober 2026 🕡 Treffen: 18:30 Uhr 🚶 Start der Tour: 18:45 Uhr pünktlich 🕘 Ende: gegen 21:00 Uhr 📍 Treffpunkt: Vor dem Handwerkerhof, nahe dem Hauptbahnhof Nürnberg 💶 Kosten: Kostenlos, wie alle unsere Aktivitäten 💬 Sprachen: Englisch & Deutsch 🙋Fragen, zum ersten Mal dabei oder unsicher wegen der Strecke? Schreib Adam StJohn Lawrence über Facebook oder WhatsApp oder kontaktiere uns über ──────────────────── 🇺🇸🇮🇳🇬🇧 Medieval Night Tour A tour through medieval Nuremberg was one of the activities people asked to try in our survey. So let’s give it a go. We will meet outside the Handwerkerhof, next to the Hauptbahnhof, and make our way through the old town towards the Imperial Castle. If you use a powered wheelchair, please make sure you have enough battery charge. The route is fairly long, includes uphill sections and passes over some cobbled streets. We will move at a relaxed pace and take time to stop, look around and talk. At the end, we will find a café, pub or another comfortable place near the castle or on the way down towards the Hauptmarkt. We can have a drink and finish the evening there. If you would prefer to join only the tour, you are of course welcome to leave before then. If the weather is bad, we will try to continue with umbrellas. Please bring your own. title: (Nü) Feder, Tinte, Gold (Kalligrafietreffen) / Quill, Ink, Gold (Calligraphy meet)
description: (English below) 🇩🇪🇦🇹🇨🇭 Am 24. Oktober haben wir etwas Besonderes vor! ✒️📜 Wir bekommen Besuch vom Bodensee: Oriane kommt zu uns und nimmt uns für einen Nachmittag mit in die Welt der historischen Kalligraphie und Buchmalerei. Egal ob ihr so etwas noch nie gemacht habt oder schon Erfahrung mit Feder und Tinte habt, ihr könnt mitmachen, ausprobieren und gemeinsam lernen. Wir schauen uns kurz an, wie Schreiben und Buchmalerei in unserer Zeitspanne funktioniert haben, welche Materialien verwendet wurden und wie man Schrift vorbereitet. Dann geht es ans Ausprobieren: Linien vorbereiten, verschiedene Schriften üben und schließlich auch etwas über Layout, Vergoldung und Malerei lernen. 📅 Samstag, 24. Oktober 🕑 14:00–17:00 Uhr, inklusive Kaffeepause 🍕 Danach können wir noch zusammensitzen und vielleicht Pizza bestellen. Ihr müsst nichts kaufen und braucht keine Vorkenntnisse. Oriane bringt zusätzliches Material zum Ausprobieren mit. Wenn ihr schon Kalligraphie-Sachen oder Vorlagen für eine Schrift habt, die ihr gerne benutzt, bringt sie gerne mit. Hilfreich sind auch Bleistifte/Druckbleistifte und, falls vorhanden, ein Zeichenbrett. Je mehr Material wir zusammenbekommen, desto weniger müssen wir teilen. Und wie immer: Wenn ihr uns noch gar nicht kennt, seid ihr genauso willkommen. Ihr müsst weder schon mittelalterliche Kalligraphie können noch sonst irgendetwas über das Mittelalter wissen. Kommt einfach dazu, probiert etwas Neues aus und lernt nebenbei ein paar von uns kennen. 😊 _________________- 🇺🇸🇮🇳🇬🇧 We have something special planned for 24 October! ✒️📜 We have a guest coming all the way from Lake Constance: Oriane is joining us for an afternoon exploring historical calligraphy and manuscript illumination. Whether you've never tried anything like this before or already have some experience with pen and ink, you can join in, experiment and learn together. We'll have a quick introduction to writing and illumination in our period, the materials that were used and how writing was prepared. Then we'll get hands-on: preparing lines, practising different hands, and learning a little about layout, gilding and painting too. 📅 Saturday, 24 October 🕑 14:00–17:00, including a coffee break 🍕 Afterwards we can hang around and order pizza if people feel like it. You don't need to buy anything and you don't need any previous experience. Oriane will bring extra materials for people to use. If you already have calligraphy equipment or exemplars for a particular hand you enjoy, please bring them along. Pencils/mechanical pencils are useful too, and if you happen to have a drawing board, bring that as well. The more equipment we have between us, the less we'll need to share. And as always, if you don't know us at all yet, you're just as welcome. You don't need to know anything about medieval calligraphy, or indeed anything about the Middle Ages. Just come along, try something new and meet a few of us while you're here. 😊

description: Shortly before the Winter's Tide, the Fall of shadows does abide and when the Harvest we hear sound, of haunts and spooks that do abound. Armigers, Lords, Ladies, Good Gentles All - Please join us for a weekend of mirth and merriment as we celebrate the harvest with a MonsTyr Bash! The Baronies of Mons Tonitrus & Tir Ysgithr invite you to Empire Ranch, Friday, October 23 through Sunday, October 25, 2026 to camp or day trip for amusing activities of both the Martial and Non-martial minded. SITE FEES Friday - Sunday Camping Adult Members $30 Adult Non-Members $40 Saturday Day Trip Only Adult Members $20 Adult Non-Members $30 Youth 17 years and under Free Preregistration will be available, but fees are the same at Gate. ACTIVITIES Hard Suit Here's a brief blurb about the melee tournament.There will be a themed melee tournament, Defeat the Headless Norseman and his minions! There will be minions, monsters, weapons and potions. Each round will have a different objective. A melee team will consist of 5 (+or- depending upon how many fighters we get) competing. The teams to be determined on the day of the tournament. Melee rules apply. Rapier HeadBall- The Headless Norseman seems to have misplaced something important. Before we give it back, how about we have some fun first? A head will be in the center of the field. Fighters will be arrayed in front of their goal posts and have the job of getting the head into the other team's goal. One hand must be empty to grab the ball. If someone is holding the ball and is disarmed or killed, the ball must be dropped. The ball can be thrown, passed, and even kicked. It's not my head, I don't mind. Objective: Get the ball in the goal. First to 5 points wins. Rez: Unlimited Hot/Cold: Cold Once, Hot with Ranged Weapons Once Light the Torches- Night is coming, and that means all that creeps in the dark is headed right towards us. Do you want monsters? You need to light torches to keep the boogens at bay, but only one team will get credit. Capture the flag scenario. Once a team flips a flag it is flipped and cannot be unflipped. Objective: Flip all three flags Rez- 2 each Hold/Cold: 2 each Let's Hunt a Monster - Have you heard the unearthly cries at night? Something is out there and it's time to take care of it. Noble townsfolk will go out into the wilderness and vanquish the terrible beast that has been tormenting the lands. One team will be hunters and their goal is to kill the Monster in 10 minutes. The other team will be the Monster and it's minions. The monster will be built out of up to 5 people. Each person will pick a weapon style and the team will determine the type of monster they are. The weapons styles should reflect the monster type as much as possible and the monster should be in mythos. Objective: Kill the Monster/Don't let them kill the monster Rez: No Duration: 10 minutes Hot/Cold: 2 hot 2 cold Archery - William Tell Shoot (Prizes to the best of the day) - Novice Shoot (Prizes to the best of the day) Thrown Weapons (Scenarios will be posted soon!) Siege Engine Demonstrations Make & Take A&S Classes - Times and Subjects to be posted soon! Vigil for Jakob inn Rammi - Friday Night Saturday Royal Court to include Jakob's answer to TRM's offer of the Order of Chivalry - Time at TRM Discretion Masked Court - To Be Announced at Their Excellencies Discretion Trick or Treating for all ages (attendees asked to bring treats for the trick or treaters - trunk or treat style) Saturday Early Evening Populace Potluck - Saturday Night - Soups, Stews, Pottages and Breads competition will provide the meal. (Prizes for best soup, stew, pottage and bread) SITE INFORMATION As this site has no shelter improvements - Please bring your own tables, chairs and shade pavilions. (Popups are allowed) If you have difficulty with mobility, we will have ADA privies and parking close to the activities. If you have an all-terrain wheelchair or walker, it will be helpful on this site as the land is dirt with low shrubs. Site is Wet. Bring Water for drinking and washing. There is no potable water on site. Site allows staking. Please pack out your own garbage. Campfires in above ground fire pits please. Please place a fire extinguisher outside of each tent. Dry RV parking is available. description: For Twelfth Night 2027, the populace is invited to celebrate a season of transition, where old traditions and joyful excess meet at the turning of the year. The theme draws inspiration from late medieval southern Germany and Switzerland, where winter observances blended seamlessly with lively seasonal celebrations marking the close of one cycle and the promise of the next. By the fifteenth century, these celebrations had fused into a distinctive blend of formality and fun. Daytime brought courtly pomp, displays of skill, and structured ceremony, while nightfall ushered in feasting, dancing, and masked revelry. This balance of order and exuberance provides the perfect setting for Atlantia’s Twelfth Night, offering a full day of pageantry and arts followed by an evening devoted to celebration, community, and unapologetic joy. During this time, the days surrounding Twelfth Night marked the end of the winter holiday season and the gradual shift toward spring. Communities gathered for pageantry, symbolic acts of renewal, and public festivities that reflected both reflection and anticipation. These moments were as much about community and tradition as they were about marking time itself. Alongside this came Fasnacht, a vibrant pre Lenten carnival that preserved much older seasonal customs. Masquerades, mummers, and playful processions filled towns with music, laughter, and satire. Masks and costumes allowed for mischief and creativity, and the rules of everyday life were happily bent before the long quiet of late winter.

description: Hail and welcome, Majesties, Excellencies, Lords, Ladies, and all good folk in between - The Barony of Starkhafn invites you to our Yule celebration! Prepare for a journey... Don your finest festive garb for an indoor and outdoor revel, and sail with us as we retrace the voyages of the Norse ancestors. From Vinland and Britannia, to the gates of Byzantium and the shores of the Caspian Sea. From Normandy to the Danelaw, and the wild Rus lands - we will explore them all! Walk amongst booths showcasing each culture (with photo opportunities for our travelers) and then feast like Jarls with a six-course banquet worthy of the sagas. The youth can anticipate Father Yule attending and bestowing gifts and pleasantries, if not a little festive entertainment. Merriment, music, and magic await. We cannot wait to celebrate with you. Skal! THE FEAST: Our Viking feast will include six courses: ● First Course: A Vinland Spread “A view into the bountiful lands and the flavors the Natives of North America would have shared.” - With cooked meats, berries, nuts, Talo flat bread, and vegetables. ● Second Course: The spoils of Old Britannia “The thick and hearty meals of the journey West, and the glory of a new land.” - Capon in Quinces (chicken stew) with shepherd’s pie and roasted vegetables. ● Third Course: Varangians in the Caspian Sea. “The flavors of Sultans and steel... The spices of a new world.” - Kubideh (seasoned ground beef) and Chicken Kabobs displayed on saffron and turmeric rice. - Bazmawurd (bread and meat wrap) with a cucumber salad and tzatziki sauce. ● Fourth Course: The raids of Normandy “The payment of conquest in Frankia, a rich and savory victory indeed.” - Beef Bourguignon (a classic French beef stew braised in red wine) ● Fifth Course: Valhalla calling me “The Saehrimnir Feast; A serving of the great boar hunted and fed upon by those in Odin's halls, only to reform and be hunted again the next day.” - Pork tenderloin with lingonberry jam and vegetables. - (Paired by request with a Lingonberry Mead brewed by Thoren Falkson of Starkhafn) ● Sixth Course: A deal with the Rus: “The succulent flavor of battles worth fighting, and a sweet treat for your Holiday pleasure.” - Ponchiki (fried dough with powdered sugar). - Honey cakes and Kissel (fruit compote) In addition to the meal, the barony will provide various sourdough breads and beverages. Any food-related allergy concerns or, if for any reason, an indoor seat is needed (indoor seating is very limited) ADDITIONAL ACTIVITIES: - Arts & Sciences at Starkhafn Yule! - HL Jerusha has a slew of activities planned for Yule: - Pentathlon Preview Display: Planning on participating in Pentathlon 2027? Show us what you have so far! Bring out your project, or, if it is not display-ready, bring your documentation and share what you have so far! There is no prize or contest, just an opportunity to share what you have and, *ONLY IF YOU WISH FOR IT*, get feedback and assistance from the assembled populace. - Traditional Arts Display: There will also be a traditional display. Bring any project that is complete or in progress; documentation is not required but encouraged. There will be prizes for Populace, Coronet, and Royal Choice. If there are any alcoholic brewing entries, they will have their own separate competition. description: Come join us, one and all for a Fun Fall Fete! Or Fall Festival of Fun, or the Fete Featuring Fall and Fun… you can pick your favourite, or come up with your own! October 31st, Barony Beyond the Mountain invites the Knowne World, or as many who are in visiting distance, to celebrate fall, have fun, and enjoy a series of activities worthy of the title of Fete! Activities will include Archery, Thrown Weapons, Heavy and Fencing lists, with various themed activities for folks of all ages, and all interests (and candy). Instead of a dayboard, we invited the attendees to bring their best and most shareable dishes! For the safety of all, please bring with you a complete list of ingredients and your own serving utensils to avoid cross contamination over multiple dishes. For further information, and to sign up to bring something, please contact Baroness Ciara. Bring your own feast gear - there is NO washing up capability on site, due to limited kitchen facilities. There will be a largess challenge (see below for details), children's activities which are open to all, and any number of good things to eat and competitions to watch throughout the day, come join us and have a marvelous October 31st in the crisp fall air! There will be a site map, as well as a scheduale for the day available at Gate. The Great BBM Largesse Challenge Baroness Ciara is once again holding her Largesse challenge. The goal of this is to inspire the populace to try a new craft, or practice their current favourite, while also donating Largesse to the kingdom and barony. This Largesse will be bestowed by Baroness Ciara and Baron Angus to those they wish to recognize. Largesse does NOT just have to be things you’ve made yourself – it can be purchased items as well. Largesse items should have a ‘look-and-feel’ representing our modern Middle Ages, but do not need to be exclusively period-informed. They can also be mundane items of use to those of us in the SCA. Donate Largesse, participate in this challenge, and be the reason someone has a great event! There will be three categories to chose from, each with a different number of items requested. The idea behind this is to encourage you to try something, work on a skill, or show off what you do very well! To that end, the three categories are: I Want To Try A Thing! For this category, please submit 4 items, preferably of a type or skill that is reasonably new to you. No one is asking you to submit a practice or your first ever attempt of a new craft! But now is the time to try out that thing that you’ve been eying. I Do This and I Want To Improve In this category, we are asking for 7 items to be displayed and donated to the barony of your choosing. This is the perfect opportunity to try your hand, and put in some practice at a skill you want to improve at! Look What I Can Do You know you know how to do this! You know the ins and outs of this item or skill or craft, and we want to see it! Come show us 13 items and display your skills with the knowledge that you are contributing to your Kingdom and Barony. If you would like to participate, and have more than 4, but less than 7, or 13, please feel free to display and donate your items. All donations are welcome. We want to see your work, and the baronage are looking forward to seeing the skills, talents and interests of their populace! Proposed Schedule of Largesse Challenge: 10:00 am – 2:00 pm – Competitors drop off Largesse at designated table. 10:00 am – 2:00 pm – Entries will be “judged” by Populace the Baron and Baroness 3:00 pm – 3:30 pm – Entrants Thank You gift pick up. Court – Winners in each of the categories below will be announced. A few Rules to follow: No food, alcohol, or edible items, not even ‘shelf stable’ items. Items may be made in a variety of methods; see the list below for ideas or come up with your own! Please include an information card attached to item of Largesse with the following information: SCA name, Home group (and Kingdom if not Eastern), as well as a short description of said item (with any possible allergens, ingredients, and/or materials.) The baronage would like to encourage the populace to appreciate the skills and goods of those who donate Largesse. To this effect, three beans will be available to the populace at the largess table, with the hope that they will visit the display of donated Largesse and place a bean with their favourite. As a thank you for participating, each participant in the display will be allowed to pick one Largesse item which has been donated, in appreciation of their hard work. description: Let the call go out that a challenge has been made! We invite all to come and join in the fun. Our current champions have served us well and are now devising devilishly fun challenges to help us decide who will win the honor of standing as our champions for the next year. We invite all to participate even if you would not stand as champion you can help to test the skills of those who would. To fulfill the role of Settmour Swamp Champion we ask that you hold no other championship title within or without our Barony. We would like to have as many as possible enjoy the spotlight and do not wish to divide loyalties by sharing with our cousins from other Baronies. If attending Pennsic next year (not a requirement) we would love to support you in representing Settmour Swamp at the Baronial champion tournaments that occur there each year. Your duties as champion are to process and stand with us in Court when present at Baronial events, to represent the Barony on the field with honor when you travel abroad, and of course to design the challenges that will help to choose your successor the following year. Our Day of Champions will be held this year at the beautiful American Legion Hall in Hackettstown. We would like to make this day a celebration of the Swamp! We invite all to come out for a day of fun, bring your projects or just come cheer on your friends. We will be having a Spread a blanket on the grass, grab a picnic table, or bring your camp chairs and enjoy the fun and fellowship of your fellow Swampies and our friends from afar. Court will immediately follow the Meet and Greet. Dayboard: Menu forthcoming Heavy Weapon tournament format: This year's Baronial Championship is fought Highlander-style: greatsword or single sword only (matching forms and no mixing weapons across the list), and the head is the only killing blow. Everything else just makes them angry. Round Robin pool play: everyone fights everyone. If more than 5 fighters enter, the field cuts to the top 4 after Round Robin. Top 4 fight single elimination, best 2 of 3, until one fighter remains. Weapons: Greatsword or single sword. Pick one form andno switching between weapon styles mid-list. Fencing Tournament Format: 1522, Autun, France. A court of the Church acquitted the rats that ravaged the barley crop. Twice, on a technicality. The village never accepted the verdict. Today, two fencers settle by the blade what the court would not. Round Robin: Best 2 of 3, every fencer against every fencer. The Final: Top two fencers meet for the championship, best 3 of 5. Choice of Form: Higher-ranked fencer chooses the weapon form for the final. Tied ranks: coin toss decides. Archery Tournament Format: Rise and shine, archers! It’s time to put your breakfast skills to the test in the Breakfast of Champions! Six arrows. One perfect breakfast. The Target: Five breakfast items, each scored once. Hit it twice, and the second shot earns nothing. Pancakes — 5 Bacon — 4 Egg — 3 Toast — 2 Coffee — 1 The Cup: A center target worth 10 points, shootable anytime — but that arrow can't also score a breakfast item. Perfect Breakfast Bonus: Hit all five items — +10 points. The Big Shot: Hit all five items with your first five arrows, then take the Cup with your sixth. Pull it off for a max score of 35. Grab your bow. Breakfast is served. Thrown Weapons Tournament Format: The barley crop lies in ruins. Rats have descended on the village stores, and the peasantry demands justice. The Church put the vermin on trial. A lawyer named Chasseneuz took their defense, arguing the accused could not appear in court without safe passage from the cats lying in wait outside. The court agreed and the trial was postponed. Then postponed again. Then postponed indefinitely so, the rats walked free. You are a peasant with a belly full of wine and an axe in your hand, and as far as you're concerned, you and your friends will take matter into your own hands. Weapons: Axes and knives (thrown). description: The Star of the Northern Army has made shields tremble and swords waver for nearly 30 years. Though he now keeps court in Valhalla, his legacy remains woven into the fabric of the East and lives on in all who pursue the call of honor and glory. Now, as we honor both his memory and the enduring legacy of those who follow in his footsteps, the Barony of Smoking Rocks once again call the populace to gather. Join us as we celebrate the return of a challenge worthy of The Silver Wyvern and mark a milestone in the history of the Barony itself. The A&S competition has been defined by the Barony’s current Champion, Layden Octavia Verita. She has specified that entries must have started within the 18 months preceding the event and documentation is not required. Please note that alcoholic beverages may not be served, sampled, or distributed as an entry for the A&S competition. Please reach out to Kadlin with any questions or comments at 302240@members.eastkingdom.org Dorstad Village is located at the beautiful Camp Haiastan, in Franklin MA. The site offers buildings that include cabins, feast hall, activity locations, and bathrooms with showers (On demand hot water!) It is also as ADA compliant as a wilderness camp can be with roads, ramps, and paths, to all locations. The site is easily accessible by highway and is within a 15-minute drive from Hotels, Banks, Restaurants, Grocery and Liquor stores! Yes, the site is discreetly damp. Please keep beverages to period drinkware and do not leave cans, bottles, or other trash around site. No yelling, “Who wants Whiskey!?!” and remember to drink responsibly or you will be asked to leave site. Cabins are furnished with bunk beds and can sleep up to four, eight, or twelve people depending on the cabin. description: Event Website: Time: 9:00 am–9:00 pm Location: Camp Herms, 1100 James Pl, El Cerrito, CA 94530 Feast Ticketing: $25.00 This year, Boar Hunt will be inspired by German Criskindtmarkt! The pre-Christian roots for these festive markets were the winter markets in the 1300’s where people stocked up for the cold season. They sold food, clothing, tools, and basic supplies needed to survive winter. In the late Middle Ages (into the 1400s–1500s,) they aligned with the Advent season and so people started buying toys, baked goods and decorations. In the 16th century, they became known as “Christkindlmarkt” or “Christ Child market.” Since these markets have such a wide historical window, we invite attendees to play in all four centuries! Perhaps we will have both Saint Nicholas and Krampus sightings! Boar Hunt is a ‘fighting event’ …mostly. There is a feast in the afternoon/evening for all in attendance. The heavy armored combatants select one of their number to serve as a ‘boar’ and the rapier combatants select a ‘stag.’ Both the boar and stag are let loose around Camp Herms while the ‘hunters’ try to dispatch it. Additionally, non-combatant attendees can serve as ‘dogs’ on the hunt! While dogs don’t fight or talk, they help locate the boar and stag for the hunters with pointing and barking. Is it silly? Maybe. Is it fun? Well, the hunt has been going on for 20+ years, so ‘yes!’ Event Steward /

Late summer across the medieval Eastern Slavic lands brought a trio of beloved feasts — the Medovyi Spas (Honey Feast), when the first honey was blessed and poppy-seed cakes shared; the Yablochnyi Spas (Apple Feast), when orchards were blessed; and the Orikhovyi or Khlibnyi Spas (Nut and Grain Feast), when the last sheaves were cut and bread baked from the new wheat. As autumn deepened, the populace turned to the Feast of the Intercession (Pokrova), honoring the protection cast over field, hearth, and folk as the world settled toward winter. The Harvest Feast of the Intercession weaves these threads together: a day of contested fields, tasted sweetness, and shared bread, closing beneath the mantle of the season’s protection. The Day’s Offerings The Field of Sheaves — Heavy Combat War Fighters take the field in a war themed to the harvest itself — companies contesting “sheaves,” “orchards,” and “hives” across the battlefield, with scenarios built around gathering, holding, and defending the harvest rather than simple slaughter. All heavy combatants authorized under Kingdom marshal rules are welcome; marshals in waiting are encouraged to lend their eyes to the lists. The Honey Cup — Mead Tasting Competition In the spirit of Medovyi Spas, brewers and vintners bring their meads — dry, sweet, melomel, metheglin, and all variations between — for populace judging. Entrants are asked to provide a brief written history or inspiration for their brew alongside tasting portions. Categories and populace’s-choice ribbons will be awarded at feast. The Bountiful Board — Cook’s Showcase Feast Rather than a single kitchen laboring alone, this feast invites individual cooks and households to contribute dishes for display and shared tasting — apple preserves, honeyed breads, roasted grains, autumn stews — each with documentation of period inspiration where possible. A populace’s-choice recognition will be given, in keeping with the spirit of sharing the first fruits of harvest. Structure ❦ Afternoon: Heavy list opens; war scenarios run through midday ❦ Early Evening: Mead tasting entries collected and judged ❦ Evening: Feast is served

title: Fighter Practice (RECURRING)
location: Caballero Park Ramada #11 (Avenue A and Desert Sun Dr), Desert Sun Dr, Yuma, AZ, 85365, United States
clean_location: Caballero Park Ramada #11 (Avenue A and Desert Sun Dr), Desert Sun Dr, Yuma, AZ, 85365, United States
description: Both Armored Combat and Rapier fighter practice are held Saturdays, 8am-10am, near Ramada #11 (SE side) of Caballero Park in Yuma, AZ. For notices of cancellation please check our calendar and our Facebook group! If you are interested in combat sports and martial arts, come give it a try! We have loaner gear available, just let us know you are interested by emailing our marshal at .org or posting to our Facebook group! Note you will want to bring your own hard-shelled sports cup (groin protection namely for males) and maybe wear long sleeved clothing. Otherwise, we have everything else you need, you just have to show up! You must be 16 and older to participate and must sign a waiver for liability purposes at every practice unless you are a paid member and authorized to fight in the SCA. Participants under 18 years old must have a parent or legal guardian present to sign a waiver and consent form. What to expect your first time at a fighter practice: We will go over all safety requirements and procedures before having you (or your parent/legal guardian) sign a waiver. Then we will help you get armored up from our loaners appropriate for armored combat or rapier, depending on your expressed interest. We then will do an armor inspection to make sure your armor meets minimum requirements and is safe. Next, we will help calibrate, which involves delivering a blow to your person to help you understand the varying degrees of force used, i.e. what is considered light, good, and excessive. We will go over some basic rules including what striking areas are legal or not. Next, we will go over and practice some basic stances and techniques to make sure you can safely deliver a blow and defend yourself. Finally, we let you have a go at it and see what you can do! Many first timers struggle with having an idea in there head of what is going to happen and executing that idea the way they pictured it. More often than not it almost never works out the way you imagined it, and that is okay! That shouldn’t discourage you from trying something that sounds cool in your head, sometimes it works out and can surprise even the most seasoned of fighters! We are all students and teachers here, even you, and we learn the most when we humble ourselves to those facts. For more information on safety and rules, please refer to the SCA Armored Combat (Rattan) Marshals Handbook and/or Atenveldt Rapier Handbook found in the Kingdom Document Library [RECURRING — also on: 3 Oct 2026, 10 Oct 2026, 17 Oct 2026, 24 Oct 2026, 31 Oct 2026, 7 Nov 2026, 14 Nov 2026, 21 Nov 2026, … 1 more through 28 Nov 2026]
